html:
SMTO-UI-0065 — Your password changed while this change was being saved

GUID: 038921a1-b21a-53f7-b3af-bd4480b564cd
Slug: portal-password-changed
Domain: UI · Subsystem: authentication

What happened

  • Another password change from this same browser, for example in a second tab, finished first. SMTO didn't apply this one, so the password from that other change is the one in effect now.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Close any other SMTO tabs or windows that show the Account page or Settings › Security › Password. Two password changes sent at the same moment from this browser caused this.
  2. Reload this page. If SMTO asks you to sign in, use the new password you typed in the other tab. The other change already took effect, so that password is the one that works now.
  3. Change your password again on the Account page only if you want a different password from the one now in effect. With no other change running, this one can be saved.
  4. If you didn't start another password change, tell your administrator right away. They can reset your password and sign out all of your sessions in case someone else is using your account.

What success looks like

  • You can sign in with the password you expect, and SMTO confirms any further change.

If it still fails

  • If none of your passwords work, ask your administrator to use Reset password on the Users page. Never send passwords or browser cookies in error reports, chat or email.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The account store found the saved password changed between verifying the current password and saving the new one, raised LoginDenied('Your password changed during this request. Try again.'), and /auth/password returned 400 without replacing the password; because resets and changes from other sessions sign this session out first, the usual cause is a second change sent with the same session cookie (another tab of this browser).

What this means

  • Another request updated the password before this change could be committed. The rejected request did not replace the saved password.

Why this can happen

  • Another request updated the password before this change could be committed.

How to diagnose it

  • The intended password change is confirmed under your current session.

How to fix it

  • This request wrote nothing; a concurrent /auth/password request carrying the same session cookie (another tab, or the Account page and Settings › Security › Password open together) saved first and kept this session signed in. Have the user reload and confirm which password now works before submitting another change; if they did not start another change, an administrator should use Reset password and Sign out all sessions for the account on the Users page (/user).
  • Sign in with the current password before submitting another change. Ask the administrator for help if you did not expect this change.

Retry and execution caution

  • Sign in with the current password before submitting another change. Ask the administrator for help if you did not expect this change.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended password change is confirmed under your current session.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained task data or repeat an operation with an unknown outcome.

Technical notes

  • Authentication guidance never changes account permissions or replays task work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
